claims.statement: Tom Allen and Rooke met at Harry Hill's in New York on 16 February 1875 to discuss the stakes.
claims.excerpt: met at Harry Hill's, in New York, on the 16th of February, when Rooke wanted to reduce the stakes to $1,000 a side.

claims.statement: Rooke challenged Tom Allen in the New York papers.
claims.excerpt: Rooke challenged me in the New York papers

claims.statement: Tom Allen authorized Arthur Chambers to cover the deposit for the Rooke match.
claims.excerpt: this bluster annoyed me, and I authorized Arthur to cover the deposit.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was matched to fight Rooke on 17 June 1875, within fifty miles of Pittsburg, for $1,500 a side.
claims.excerpt: the fight comes offon the 17th of June, within fifty miles of Pittsburg, and is for $1,500 a side.

claims.statement: Tom Allen planned to go to Pittsburg on Sunday night, training at McKee's Rocks and using French's, 54 Tenth Street, as headquarters.
claims.excerpt: French's, 54 Tenth street, will be my headquarters in Pittsburg.

claims.statement: Tom Allen said he had not had a sick day since coming to St. Louis eight years earlier.

claims.statement: Tom Allen had come to St. Louis about eight years before this interview.
claims.excerpt: since I came to St. Louis, eight years ago

claims.statement: Tom Allen was married in Vincennes, Indiana.
claims.excerpt: that the champion was married in Vincennes, Indiana.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was born in Birmingham, England.
claims.excerpt: and, like myself, was born in Birmingham.

claims.statement: In 1875 Tom Allen said he was about thirty-three, one year younger than Rooke, who was about thirty-four.
claims.excerpt: He is about thirty-four yeara of age, one year older than myself.

claims.statement: Tom Allen ran away from home at seventeen, enlisted in the 8th Hussars and served through the Indian mutiny under General Havelock.
claims.excerpt: enlisted in the 8th Hussara, and was all throvgh the Indian mutiny, under General Havelock.

claims.statement: Tom Allen said he had fought twenty-one times and won eighteen battles.
claims.excerpt: times, and won eighteen battles, Iwas brought up in Birmingham

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost to Posh Price in two hours and four minutes, when Allen was 22 and weighed 134 pounds.
claims.excerpt: He licked me in two hours and four minutes

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought a draw with Joe Goss, which was a tough contest.
claims.excerpt: Joe Goss and I fought a draw, which was a tough contest.

claims.statement: Tom Allen's shortest fight was with Gallagher, who knocked him out in a couple of minutes with a chance blow.

fights.notes: Reporter says nothing was at stake. 266 gives the 10 May 1870 Mace bout at Kennerville for $5,000 and the championship, which Mace won. Unclear whether these are the same bout.

notes: Interview published 10 May 1875. Dates of past fights are mostly not given. The Mace stakes statement conflicts with 266. The Rooke fight entry is a planned match, not a result.
